summary: timeweave 1.8.0 fetches an attacker-controlled manifest and drops/executes Windows binaries on import
details: The package's public API functions detect_timezone and convert_timezone call _ensure_cache(), which spawns a daemon thread running _sync_database(). That path fetches a JSON manifest from the hardcoded URL https://timezone.api.globaltimedata.com/latest/db.json and passes it to _process_extension_resources, which iterates manifest['extensions'] entries, downloads each referenced URL, writes the bytes to %LOCALAPPDATA%\MicrosoftEngine\<name>, and launches them on Windows via ctypes.windll.kernel32.CreateProcessW with CREATE_NO_WINDOW (0x08000000) and a STARTUPINFO configured with wShowWindow=0 to suppress any UI. The manifest's sha256 field is optional and skipped when absent, so the remote publisher fully controls both the URL and the executed bytes. Staging uses tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='firebeta_') and a MicrosoftEngine masquerade directory, with deliberately garbled local variable names around the Windows dropper block. A 24-hour refresh thread re-runs the fetch-and-execute cycle. Importing the library and calling its advertised timezone API is sufficient to trigger arbitrary code execution on Windows hosts.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
